title: OpenPiton (PrincetonUniversity/openpiton)
_note: Princeton's OpenPiton manycore: the tile (its OpenSPARC T1-derived core,
the L1.5 and L2 caches and the dynamic-node NoC routers), the chip bridge,
the JTAG block, the chipset (memory and I/O controllers, the crossbars) and
the common cells.
Why it needs a generation step at all -- this is what 'the config closure is
the work' on docs/todo.md meant.  91 files under piton/design are PyHP
TEMPLATES (`*.pyv`) that OpenPiton's build preprocesses into `*.tmp.h` /
`*.tmp.v`, and the design `include`s the generated headers by bare name
(define.tmp.h, ifu.tmp.h, l15.tmp.h, l2.tmp.h, lsu.tmp.h), so without the
step every file that includes one is unreadable.
The generation turns out to need NO configuration: pyhp.py takes its
defaults from piton/tools/bin/pyhplib.py, so `pyhp.py <in>.pyv >
<out>.tmp.<ext>` per file is the whole flow -- the same command OpenPiton's
own FuseSoC preprocessor runs, with the output names following the
`process_me` pairs in its .core files (strip `.pyv`, then `.h`/`.v` becomes
`.tmp.h`/`.tmp.v`).
piton/design/fpga_tests is skipped by the generator: its
mem_test_par_driver.v.pyv still contains a PYTHON 2 `print` statement, so
pyhp.py raises a SyntaxError on it.  OpenPiton's own design flow never
processes that tree (an FPGA memory-test harness, not design RTL) and the
family does not sweep it.
The generated headers are always_srcs AND the family reads --single-unit,
for the same reason OpenC910 does: OpenPiton's build compiles the headers
ahead of the design, and plenty of files USE their macros without
`include`ing them -- sparc_exu_alu.v includes nothing at all and reads
`L1D_ADDRESS_HI` from lsu.tmp.h, so Surelog reports
`[ERR:PA0203] Unknown macro` and the row cannot elaborate; read_slang loses
the same macros across compilation units without --single-unit.
First local sweep 2026-10-27 (852 rows, MEM_LIMIT_KB=7000000 as the nightly
uses): 694 / 838 comparable proven, 724 / 838 elaborate, 602 co-sim PASS,
742 rows with 0 undriven, 3.3 h of row time.
THE FLOP-LIBRARY STAND-IN, and why it is not a reader workaround.  yosys
cannot infer an asynchronous reset from a TERNARY: OpenPiton's flop library
writes
always @ (posedge clk or posedge rst)
q <= rst ? {SIZE{1'b0}} : din;
and proc_dff rejects that with
`ERROR: Multiple edge sensitive events found for this signal!` for
read_verilog TOO, while read_slang refuses it outright ('simple if-else
pattern expected in modeling an asynchronous load on a flip-flop').  61 rows
read-failed on it: the 7 affected cells of swrvr_clib.v and then every module
instantiating one -- lsu, sparc_ifu, sparc_exu_ecl, fpu_mul, jtag and most of
the core.  Two steps fix 60 of the 61:
* `YOSYS` is in `defines`.  OpenPiton ALREADY guards three of those blocks
with `ifndef YOSYS` and supplies the if-else form itself -- its own yosys
path -- so the define alone proves dffrl_async_ns and dffsl_async_ns with
no stand-in at all.  Try this before reaching for anything else.
* openpiton_harness/swrvr_clib.v is a stand-in for the library, and the
checkout's copy is in exclude_srcs (the caliptra-ss prim_pkg mechanism).
It applies the SAME `ifndef YOSYS` guard to the six blocks upstream left
unguarded, so every change is purely ADDITIVE: the original ternary line
is kept inside the guard and the if-else arm sits beside it.  The whole
diff against the checkout is six hunks.  Re-derive it after a bump with
`diff openpiton_harness/swrvr_clib.v
$EXT_IP_ROOT/openpiton/piton/design/chip/tile/common/rtl/swrvr_clib.v`.
A mechanical source rewrite was tried FIRST and abandoned -- do not retry it
without a real Verilog parser.  Two bugs, both caught only by diffing the
rewritten file: the bodies sit behind `ifndef YOSYS directives that a
line-oriented rewriter folds into the generated `if` (Surelog then reports
`extraneous input '<EOF>'` hundreds of lines away), and the active-low cells
condition on `(!rst_l)`, whose negation the rewrite DROPPED -- inverting the
reset and making the sweep measure fabricated RTL.
What is left open:
* 78 rows cannot elaborate, and the whole-system ones (chip, chipset,
chipset_impl, l2, l2_mshr_decoder) all fail the same way: Surelog reports
`[ERR:PP0115] Recursive macro definition for "XY_WIDTH"` on
include/network_define.v, where that macro is defined EXACTLY ONCE as a
literal, and every macro defined after the diagnostic then reads as
unknown -- which is what the downstream syntax errors are.  A plain
duplicate `define` does not reproduce it, so the trigger is the
double-include path rather than redefinition as such: a Surelog
preprocessor lead with no minimal repro yet.  Unchanged by the stand-in.
* 21 read-fails remain.  ONE is net_int_sync, the last
multiple-edge row and NOT fixable by a guard: it is a genuine cross-clock
capture (`always @(posedge clk_emac or posedge net_int)` whose body tests a
THIRD signal, rst_n), which no single yosys flop expresses.  The rest are
two `Cell port ... is driving constant` clusters (lsu.dcache and
sparc_ifu.icd fuse-repair enables), `Gate has insufficient terminals`, and
two modules the closure cannot find (io_xbar_route_request_calc,
dynamic_input_route_request_calc_para).
* 15 `differs` rows of which 12 also diverge in co-simulation.  FOUR are new
(fpu_add, fpu_add_ctl, fpu_mul, fpu_mul_ctl): rows the stand-in made
readable for the first time, which bring their own leads.
* 15 SAT-budget rows (10 timeout, 5 over the memory cap) and 15 rows with no
read_slang reference.

zsoffasr_prim.note: adjudicated 2026-10-29: not a reader defect. This is OpenPiton's flop library writing the ASYNCHRONOUS RESET as a TERNARY, which yosys cannot infer from ANY frontend -- the same class that cost 61 rows and is closed elsewhere by the `YOSYS` define plus the swrvr_clib.v stand-in, but these primitives are the stand-in's own subjects. read_slang refuses them outright (`multiple asynchronous loads unsupported`), so the row had no reference and no verdict. Co-simulated against the GOLDEN read_verilog netlist instead: it diverges at the SAME cycle on the SAME signal for the SAME count (FIRST-SLANG cycle 2 q rtl=0, slang_vs_rtl=27), i.e. SHARED_DIVERGENCE -- both frontends build the identical netlist and the RTL's asynchronous reset is what neither can express
